title: A Guide to Credible Financial News Sources and Platforms
content:
Developing healthy financial literacy requires cultivating reliable, high-integrity information sources while filtering out speculative social media hype.

Credible financial news platforms are divided into primary data providers and professional financial journalism:

1. Primary Regulatory Data: The ultimate source of corporate truth is the SEC EDGAR system (sec.gov/edgar). Here, investors can read official, audited annual reports (10-K), quarterly reports (10-Q), and insider trading forms (Form 4) directly from the issuing companies. For economic metrics, the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis maintains FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data), a free database of hundreds of thousands of historical economic indicators.

2. Real-Time Financial Wire Services: Bloomberg News and Reuters are world-renowned for rapid, unbiased factual reporting of international market events, corporate earnings, and policy changes without sensationalist spin.

3. In-Depth Business Journalism: The Wall Street Journal and The Financial Times offer comprehensive editorial analysis, investigative reporting on corporate governance, and macro economic perspectives.

4. Free Retail Market Platforms: Yahoo Finance, Google Finance, and Investopedia provide excellent free access to real-time quotes, financial statements, and educational articles explaining complex concepts.

Avoid relying on anonymous social media trading forums, hype channels, and 'get-rich-quick' influencers who promote volatile micro-cap stocks or high-risk options schemes.
